raw_response:
I'm 67 this year, and I've been farming this land since I was 22. Never went to school — can't read a word — but my mother and father taught me everything, and after 45 years I know every corner of these 15 mu. My family is just three of us now: me, my old man, and our daughter-in-law when she's not working at the garment factory in town. We're getting on, so the heavy carrying and bending is harder than it used to be, but we still manage.

Last year I kept 8 mu for wheat then maize, 4 mu for cotton, 2 mu for peanut, and 1 mu for mungbean on the corner plot. The wheat did okay, about 800 jin per mu, and the maize was good too — nearly 1,000 jin per mu. Cotton gave steady money but picking it four times wore out my knees. Peanut prices were decent at the market in Quzhou town. So this year I'm not changing much. Change is risky when you're my age. But fertilizer prices are high again, and I talked to my neighbor Auntie Liu — she cut back her wheat fertilizer a little last year and said the yield was almost the same. So I'll do a bit less too, save some money for medicine.

For the wheat I'm planting now: I'll use my own saved seed from last year's best big heads — no cost there. For fertilizer, I'll spread about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, that's around 40 jin per mu. Then in spring, if the wheat looks yellow at green-up, I'll topdress with about 25 jin of urea per mu. If it looks strong and green, maybe I do less or skip it. Water from the well costs electricity, so I'll irrigate three times: once after planting to help it settle, once in spring when it wakes up, and once at grain filling if it's dry. No more — I can't waste that money.

For maize next summer: right after wheat harvest in early June, I have to plant fast — sometimes only five or six days before the season turns. I'll buy hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. I'll put compound fertilizer in the holes when planting, about 30 jin per mu, and if rain comes I might add a little urea when the plants are knee-high. I'll irrigate once or twice depending on the rain. Last year twice was enough.

Cotton: I'll plant in late April on the same 4 mu. Cotton needs picking four or five times, which is hard on my back. My daughter-in-law helps, but if there's too much boll I hire local women for picking — I already know I'll need maybe ten days of hired help at harvest. I'll put down about 30 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. Irrigate twice — once when flowering, once when the bolls are fat.

Peanut: 2 mu, plant in early May. Peanut doesn't need much feeding — about 20 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and keep the weeds down. One irrigation should do if the summer rains are normal.

Mungbean: Just 1 mu, thrown in on the small plot after the wheat comes off in late June. Mungbean is easy — almost no fertilizer, maybe one watering. Grows fast, harvest by late August.

Money is tight. I have about four or five thousand yuan for all inputs this year. The wheat, peanut, and mungbean seed is my own, but maize seed I must buy. Fertilizer is the biggest cost. I try not to hire much labor except for cotton picking and a few days at wheat and maize harvest if my nephew isn't free to help. Every yuan I spend on the field is a yuan I don't have for doctor visits or fixing the roof.
